equinix-amer-p11-eqx-q3-2026-earnings-pr.summary: Equinix's Q3 2026 earnings presentation (49 slides), linked from its results release of 28 October 2026 for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. Slide 35, 'Data Center Portfolio Composition - AMER', lists for the metro Washington DC/Ashburn sixteen IBX data centers: Stabilized DC1, DC3, DC4, DC5, DC6, DC10, DC11, DC12, DC13, DC14, DC15, DC21 and DC97; Expansion DC2 and DC16; New DC22; Owned DC1, DC2, DC4, DC5, DC6, DC11, DC12, DC13, DC14, DC15, DC16, DC21 and DC22; Leased DC3, DC10 and DC97. For Miami it lists four: Stabilized MI2, MI3 and MI6; Expansion MI1; Owned MI1 and MI6; Leased MI2 and MI3. For Montreal it lists two: Expansion MT1 and MT2, both owned. The Americas change summary names only TR4 (Toronto) as a closed IBX. Slide 47 defines Stabilized Data Centers as those whose final expansion or redevelopment phase began operating before 1 January 2025, Expansion Data Centers as those whose Phase 1 began operating before 1 January 2025 with an expected expansion of one or more additional phases (or a redevelopment, or a new phase opened on or after 1 January 2025), and New Data Centers as those whose Phase 1 began operating on or after 1 January 2025. Slide 30 reports Q3 2026 cabinets billed and recurring revenues for the 193 stabilized, 52 expansion and 12 new IBX data centers (257 in all). The presentation thus states that DC3, DC12, DC15, DC16, DC21, DC22, MI6 and MT1 were operating Equinix IBX data centers at the quarter end, 30 September 2026, with DC3 leased and the others owned. No address, capacity per IBX or opening date is given.

Slide 37, 'Data Center Portfolio Composition - APAC', lists 65 APAC IBX data centers by metro and category. Slide 47 defines Stabilized Data Centers as those whose final expansion or redevelopment phase began operating before 1 January 2025. Slide 30 reports Q3 2026 cabinets billed and recurring revenues for the 193 stabilized IBX data centers. The presentation thus states that SG2, SG3, SY1, SY2, SY3 and SY4 are operating Equinix IBX data centers in its portfolio for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. It gives no address, capacity per IBX or opening date.

ntt-gdc-p11-nttdata-q2-fy2026-presentati.summary: NTT DATA Group's company presentation for the Q2 FY2026 results briefing (23 slides; cover dated November 4, 2026; English translation of the Japanese original). FY2026 runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027 (slide 2). Slide 11, 'Overseas Segment - Investments and Operating Results for the DC Business', states that cumulative investments for H1 FY2026 totaled $1,358 million, 'with service launches in Phoenix, Dallas, and Virginia in the U.S., and Amsterdam in Europe'. Its Total Power Capacity chart gives approximately 1,630 MW as of 31 March 2026 (North America 675, EMEA 430, India 425, APAC 100) and approximately 1,755 MW as of 30 September 2026 (Results: North America 780, EMEA 450, India 425, APAC 100); footnote 1 says data centres transferred to NTT DC REIT continue to be operated by the Group and are included. Slide 21 gives H1 FY2026 (April-September) new capacity of 125 MW and current capacity as of 30 September 2026 of 1,755 MW. The presentation thus states that NTT's data-centre business launched service in its Phoenix, Dallas and Amsterdam markets during the half year ended 30 September 2026, i.e. that NTT data-centre capacity in each of these markets was in service at that date. It does not name the building, campus phase or capacity of each launch, and it gives no opening date.

rf-4-p12-middlesex-bos-2026-10-30-minute.summary: The township's minutes of the Board of Supervisors workshop meeting held on 30 October 2026 record public comment on the ongoing impacts of PAX-1 construction on Country Club Road residents (noise, dust, blasting-related damage claims) and of construction work heard after 7 p.m. the previous evening. The board's vice-chairman acknowledged the negative impacts of construction on Country Club Road residents, said he continues to press the developer to buy out or compensate residents living adjacent to the construction site, and agreed to contact the developer about the evening work. The township engineer reported Country Club Road repairs to be made under the PAX-1 developer's agreement, and the board discussed newly planted PAX-1 landscaping. The board also granted the developer's request to extend the review time for the Final Land Development Plans for Pennsylvania Digital (PAX-1) Phase 1-C and Phase 2 to 3 February 2027 to allow redesign (closed-loop cooling and battery backup power were mentioned), and discussed the county reassessment of the 694-acre PAX-1 property.

us-colo-reits-p11-irm-q3-2026-supplement.summary: Iron Mountain's Q3 2026 Supplemental Financial Information (29 pages; Workiva PDF created 5 November 2026), released with its third-quarter results on 5 November 2026 for the quarter ended 30 September 2026. Page 22, 'Data Center Operating Portfolio', lists by market the facilities in its operating portfolio with Stabilized, Pre-Stabilized and Total leaseable MW and leased %: Phoenix rows 'AZP-1' 41.0 MW, 'AZP-2' 46.5 MW and 'AZP-3 (1)' 36.0 MW (each Stabilized, 100.0% leased); Denver row 'DEN-1' 11.3 MW (Stabilized, 86.0% leased); Chicago row 'CHI-1' 12.0 MW (Stabilized, 100.0% leased); also Scottsdale AZS-1 5.7 MW, Boyers and Other 'WPA-1 and Other' 14.2 MW, New Jersey NJE-1 20.8 MW, Miami MIA-1 16.0 MW and Northern Virginia VA-1 to VA-7. Footnote (1): AZP-3, VA-4/5, VA-6 and VA-7 are held by consolidated joint ventures. The same page gives Total Potential Capacity of 544.6 MW in the Operating Portfolio, 317.1 MW Under Construction and 511.9 MW Held for Development. Page 23, 'Data Center Expansion and Development Activity', has no Phoenix or Denver row; its Chicago row 'CHI-1 Future Phases (1)' (24.0 MW pre-leased) carries the footnote 'Includes megawatts pre-leased where construction is planned, but has not commenced'. The definitions page defines Pre-Stabilized as 'A building recently placed in service which has not yet reached 85% leased or 24 months in service' and Leaseable MW as critical power capacity available for customer use. The operating-portfolio rows are thus Iron Mountain's dated statement that AZP-1, AZP-2, AZP-3, DEN-1 and CHI-1 were in service in its operating portfolio at 30 September 2026. No address, opening date or building outline is given.
